newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard hopes wages prompt Australia rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard hopes wages prompt Australia rate cut.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday he hoped forthcoming wages data would prompt a monetary policy easing.

"I would hope that if the wages figures today are broadly in line with what the Reserve Bank regards as satisfactory, I would hope that they, the bank -- it controls these matters -- would see its way clear for a further cut in rates," Howard said on Sydney radio station 2UE.
"But that's a matter ultimately for the bank," Howard said.
"But we have got 1960s levels of inflation in Australia. Now that's unqualifiedly good news for this country."
On July 31 the Reserve Bank eased monetary policy for the first time in three years, cutting its overnight cash rate target to 7.0 percent from 7.5 percent.
Inflation data issued on Wednesday showed underlying consumer prices -- excluding irregular items -- had risen 2.4 percent between the September quarters of 1995 and 1996.
August wages data will be issued at 0130 GMT (11.30 a.m.).
